# Every spend record lacks `seq`, `kind` and `crc`, so the rule the log is written under already classifies each one as torn

`domains/modus/cost/0001.ndjson` is an append-only log under `doc:40-durability#append-only-log`
— `doc:60-cost-model#spend-record` says so in its own first sentence, and §2.2's preamble names
*"cost events"* among the data the shape is for, so the spend ledger is inside the scope of the
rules below and not beside it (E1).

§2.2.3 requires *"a monotonic `seq` (per log), an ISO-8601 UTC `at`, and a `kind`"* of every
record. §2.2.5 requires *"`crc`, the CRC-32C of the record's canonical serialisation with the
`crc` field itself omitted"*, and adds *"`crc` is the last key."* Neither record committed at
`0e4324d` carries `seq`, `kind` or `crc`, and neither does any of the 287 records in the primary
checkout's working tree at `2026-09-04T09:24:23Z` (E2). They are not computed and then dropped —
established over a search that finds hits rather than one that finds none: the words `crc`,
`CRC` and `crc32` occur zero times in `tools/cost-record.py` and `tools/cost_lib.py`, and a
second search by **different** words turns up six `hashlib` lines, all of which are a replay's
input provenance or a lock filename and none of which reaches a record (E3).

The consequence is not that a check has nothing to operate on. It is the opposite. §2.2.6:

> A record whose line does not parse, **lacks `crc`**, or whose recomputed `crc` does not match
> is **torn**: it is skipped on read, reported, and the log is marked `degraded` (§7). It is
> never repaired and never silently dropped.

Every line in the ledger lacks `crc`. By §2.2.6 the whole file is already torn.

## §2.2.6 and §7 disagree, on exactly this case

§2.2.6 does not carry its own consequence. It delegates — *"the log is marked `degraded` (§7)"* —
and §7 is the section that specifies the recovery pass an implementer actually writes.
**§7's condition table does not contain the case §2.2.6 sends to it.** The table enumerates
nine conditions and the enumeration is complete, which is what lets absence be read off it
(E10). Its three log rows are: a truncated final line, a *"Log line that fails to parse, or
whose `crc` does not match"*, and a *"Log with a `seq` gap"*. A record that lacks `crc`
neither fails to parse nor mismatches. The word *lacks* occurs exactly once in the whole
document — §2.2.6, line 102 (E10).

So the sentence this bean carried in review — that a correct reader of §7 skips the whole file
by the `crc` route — does not follow from §7. It follows from §2.2.6 alone, and §2.2.6 has no
recovery pass to be implemented from.

**The conclusion survives by a different row.** No record carries `seq` either, so §7's
`seq`-gap row — *"Log with a `seq` gap | Log at ERROR; mark the log degraded; do not silently
renumber"* — is a route to `degraded` that §7 does contain, and it degrades the whole log
rather than one record. It is the shorter step of the two, because the parse/mismatch row
enumerates two conditions and absence satisfies neither, while the `seq` row names a property
of the log. It is not a free step: §7 says *a gap*, and a log in which **no** record carries
`seq` has no sequence for a gap to sit in. Whichever way that is read, it is read rather than
specified.

This is a defect in `doc:40-durability`, not only in the ledger, and it is worth more than the
missing fields: two sections of the document that owns torn-record detection disagree about the
condition, and the disagreement is invisible unless you hold both open. Criterion 7 cannot be
closed until they are reconciled, and criterion 1's three candidate answers each imply a
different reconciliation — so the reconciliation is the same decision, not extra work.

## The reader that does exist, and what it does with a line it cannot parse

`tools/cost-record.py`'s `last_record_for` is the only code in the tree that reads this log. It
is the billing cursor: `Stop` fires per turn, each record is a delta, and the previous record's
`lastMessageId` is where the next one starts. On a line that does not parse it executes
`except ValueError: continue` — skipped, not reported, nothing marked `degraded` (E5). That is
the clause of §2.2.6 it violates, and `crc` is not needed to violate it.

What the skip costs is money. `advance_cursor`'s own docstring names the outcome it was rewritten
to prevent — a missing cursor falling back to billing every message, *"which silently re-bills
the run from its first message into an append-only money log"* — and says *"never that one"*.
But `previous is None` still returns `(messages, "full", None)`, and
`last_record_for` returns `None` for a run whose only record it silently skipped. Driven through
the real functions against a scratch log, four separate damage shapes each turn the cursor into
`None` and `advance_cursor` then bills every message it was handed (E6). The guard is in the
function that consumes the cursor; the hole is in the function that produces it.

Four producers reach a damaged line, and none is hypothetical here.

- A crash between `os.write` and `os.fsync` leaves a **truncated final line with no trailing
  newline**. This is not a torn record: §2.2.7 makes it the *only* permitted repair — *"discarded
  on read and truncated away before the next append"* — explicitly discarded rather than torn.
  That is what makes it the sharpest case rather than the weakest. Even the behaviour
  `doc:40-durability` calls **correct** throws the record away, and throwing it away is exactly
  what loses the cursor. There is no reading of §2.2.7 under which the money is safe; criterion 5
  therefore has to answer for the documented-correct path too, not only for the broken one.
- A **hand merge**. `bean:0117` records that every branch touching this file conflicts at its
  last line and that it is merged by hand today; losing the newline that joins two records is
  the cheapest damage a hand merge can do, and it produces a line that does not parse.
- A **conflict marker left in the file** — a line that does not parse, in a log whose only reader
  discards such lines without a word.
- An **interleaved partial write from a second appender**, which `doc:40-durability` §4.2 says in
  terms the lock does not protect against: *"Nothing about a second process or a hand-editing
  human."* Two worktrees appending at once is the ordinary condition of this repository.

Two further things the finding did not contain, beyond the §2.2.6/§7 disagreement above.

- **The log carries three record shapes and nothing distinguishes them.** One `append` call
  writes the spend record, one writes a `billingBasis: refused` line with `billed: false`, and
  one writes an error line whose `at` is `None` (E7). `kind` is exactly the discriminator
  §2.2.3 asks for; without it a consumer must sniff keys, and the rollups
  `doc:60-cost-model` §3.3 specifies would fold three different things together.
- **`crc` as the last key is incompatible with how the writer serialises.** `append` uses
  `json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True)`, under which `crc` sorts between `costUsdDisplay` and
  `cwd` (E8). §2.2.5's *"`crc` is the last key"* and §8's *"stable frontmatter key order"*
  canonicalisation therefore have to be reconciled before a `crc` can be both written and
  recomputed on read. That is a decision this work has to take, not a detail of it.

## Why this is a work item and not an observation

The bar is whether it changes what someone does.

- A damaged line in this log re-bills money already billed, into a file that is append-only and
  therefore cannot be corrected in place. **Which re-bill you get depends on how many records the
  run has**, and the bean previously claimed only the worse half. A re-bill *of the run in full*
  needs every record for that run to be unreadable; with an intact earlier record the cursor
  falls back to it and you get a **partial** double-bill of everything between the two. Both
  outcomes were driven through the real functions, for each of the four producers above (E6). On
  the live ledger 33 of 51 runs carry exactly one record, so the full case is the majority and
  the partial case is the rest (E11). `bean:0054` built the refusal path to stop the full
  outcome; it is reachable only through a cursor the same file discards without reporting, and
  it never sees the partial one at all.
- **It is not fully silent, and what makes it audible is free.** `build_record` writes
  `"billingBasis": billing_basis` straight from `advance_cursor`, so a re-bill after a lost
  cursor is stamped `billingBasis: "full"` — ambiguous with a legitimate first record, but not
  unrecorded. That yields a detector needing no new field and no new writer: *a `full` record
  that is not the first for its `runId`*. Run against the live ledger it returns nothing —
  287 records, 51 stamped `full`, 51 distinct `runId`s, **0** that are not first (E11). The
  defect is reachable and has not yet fired, which is the observed-not-yet-failing baseline
  criterion 6 asks for and is a more useful statement than either "it is broken" or "it is fine".
- Every merge of this file is a hand merge today (`bean:0117`), and a hand merge is the cheapest
  way in the repository to produce a line that does not parse.
- `bean:0017` will build a reader that, applied to this file as it stands, marks the spend
  ledger `degraded` in its entirety on the first startup — by §7's `seq`-gap row, since §7 has no
  row for the `crc` absence §2.2.6 sends it. Whether that is the right outcome, or whether the
  existing records are grandfathered, is a decision someone has to take, and it cannot be taken
  before §2.2.6 and §7 are made to agree. Taking either after the adapter ships is more expensive
  than taking both now.

None of the seven is blocked by this and this is blocked by none of them, so no `blocked_by`
edge is added. The sequencing note against `bean:0017` is a note, not an edge: `bean:0017` can
be built without this and would then be built against a ledger it must reject.

Criterion 3 was written as a co-decision with `bean:0117`, which contradicted that: a criterion
that cannot be satisfied until another `todo` bean answers **is** an edge, whatever the paragraph
above says. It is reworded one-directionally rather than edged, so the two statements agree. The
reason is that the dependency only runs one way. This bean has to settle what a *per-log*
monotonic `seq` means for a file appended to from many worktrees, and it has to settle it
whether or not `bean:0117` ever weighs `merge=union`; `bean:0117` is then bound by the answer,
because a merge strategy cannot be chosen for a field whose semantics are undecided. An edge in
the direction the old wording implied would have this bean waiting on the bean that is waiting
on it.

## The counter-argument this bean has to answer, and does not defeat itself with

Criterion 1 offers *"amend `doc:40-durability` §2.2 to state the exception a harness-edge log
gets"* as a candidate answer. The two nearest things in the corpus to such an exception both
exist, and neither is one (E12).

- **`doc:60-cost-model` §3.2.1, "What a harness-edge recorder can supply".** It is a real,
  measured relaxation for a recorder at the `Stop`/`SubagentStop` edge — but of **§3.2's field
  list**, which is the cost model's own table of business fields. Every field it excuses is one
  the harness cannot observe: `stage`, `workItemId`, `rationale`, `priceBookEntryId`. `seq`,
  `kind` and `crc` are not observations of anything; they are properties of the *write*, which
  the writer performs and therefore knows. §3.2.1 does not reach §2.2 and would not excuse them
  if it did.
- **`adr:0006-framework-boundary#classification` places `tools/` at tier 3**, this domain's own
  workflow. That is a statement about who owns the *writer*, and it is the strongest form of the
  worry: if `tools/` is this domain's business, why does a framework document bind it? Because
  the rule is not addressed to the writer. `doc:40-durability`'s `read_when` matches
  `**/*.ndjson` — the **file**, not the tool — and §2.2 is a contract between whoever writes such
  a file and whoever reads it. `bean:0017`'s reader is tier 1 and will read this tier-3 writer's
  output. A tier-3 tool may decide whether to keep an append-only log; having chosen to keep one
  at a path §3's layout diagram names, it does not get to redefine the shape.

Both are therefore answered rather than dismissed, and neither weakens the finding. Recording
them is the point: a bean that asks whether an exception exists has to name the two documents a
later reader will find and think it did.

records up to §2.2, amend §2.2 to state the exception, or move the ledger out of §2.2's scope —
is the first thing the work has to settle, so no criterion presumes one.

There were ten. The struck one read *"`bean:0054` and `bean:0068` are not edited; both are
`completed`"*, and it restated `docs-lint` check 11, whose header says it in the same words —
*"A completed bean is final except for appended amendments"*, classifying each changed bean by
the `status:` it has on the merge base (`tools/docs-lint.sh:305`, E13). Criterion 9 was therefore
satisfied by running criterion 10, which is now criterion 9. A criterion a gate already enforces
mechanically is a criterion nobody checks (`doc:00-constitution#mechanical-enforcement`). It also
named `bean:0068`, which this bean draws nothing else from; that reference now survives only as
the quotation above, and the PR body's `refs:` lists it on that basis rather than as a source.

## Evidence — the finding, verified rather than relayed

Taken at `ab7137b`, this branch's head, with `/usr/bin/grep` — BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD, the
implementation CI has. The interactive shell in this environment resolves `grep` to
`ugrep 7.8.4`, a different program; step 0 prints the version of `$G` and of the shell's own
`grep` so a reader can see which one produced every hit below. Nothing here ran through the
alias.

Corpus figures name `0e4324d` explicitly rather than reading the working tree, so this file
being added to `.beans` cannot change any of them (`doc:50-memory-and-evidence#corpus-figures`).
The two figures that are not corpus figures — steps 5 and 16, over the primary checkout's
ledger — are stamped with the clock instead, because their subject is a tree that is changing by
design, including by the run that took them; `bean:0117` E3 is the record of that growth being
watched, and it is not re-measured here.

PR #69 owns `tools/` and will falsify every line number in steps 6 to 9, 12 and 19 when it
merges. Re-running them belongs to that merge.

**This capture replaces the one taken at `0e4324d`, which had three wrong figures.** They are
re-taken rather than patched, because a line corrected inside a fence is no longer a capture
(`doc:50-memory-and-evidence#capturing`): E7's attribution of the three `append` call sites,
which also miscounted its own paste; E2's *"differing only by `parentRunId`"*, contradicted by
its own step-4 output four lines above it; and E3's claim of absence, which searched twice with
the same word and carried no control.

The script writes nothing inside the repository. Step 15's only writes are under `$SCRATCH`,
asserted positively and negatively in its first two output lines, and step 20 is the check from
the other side: `git status --porcelain` over `domains`, `tools`, `documentation` and
`build.gradle.kts` in the worktree the script ran in.

```
#!/bin/bash
# Read-only against the repository. Corpus figures name 0e4324d explicitly, so this file
# being added to .beans cannot change its own subject (doc:50-memory-and-evidence#corpus-figures).
# Steps 5 and 16 read the primary checkout's ledger, which is changing by design, so they are
# stamped with the clock instead. Step 15 writes only under $SCRATCH; step 19 proves it.
cd /Users/maxholman/IdeaProjects/Modus/.claude/worktrees/agent-a2ffaae02565140c5 || exit 9
G=/usr/bin/grep
P=/Users/maxholman/IdeaProjects/Modus/domains/modus/cost/0001.ndjson
SCRATCH=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxholman-IdeaProjects-Modus/ffd4977c-3d34-41e9-a3ae-f60919540688/scratchpad/fakerepo

echo "=== 0. tree, clock, and which grep — every \$G below is /usr/bin/grep, the one CI has"
git rev-parse HEAD
date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ
$G --version | head -1
command grep --version | head -1

echo "=== 1. what doc:40 §2.2 requires, and of which logs"
sed -n '84,86p;97,105p' documentation/40-durability.md

echo "=== 2. the layout entry that names this file"
$G -n 'cost/0001.ndjson' documentation/40-durability.md

echo "=== 3. what doc:60 §3.2 calls it"
sed -n '148,151p' documentation/60-cost-model.md

echo "=== 4. keys of every distinct record shape, committed at 0e4324d"
git show 0e4324d:domains/modus/cost/0001.ndjson | python3 -c '
import sys, json, collections
s = collections.Counter()
n = 0
for l in sys.stdin:
    l = l.strip()
    if not l: continue
    n += 1
    s[frozenset(json.loads(l))] += 1
print("records:", n)
for k, v in s.items():
    print(v, "record(s), %d keys:" % len(k), sorted(k))
a, b = sorted(s, key=len)
print("the two shapes differ by exactly:", sorted(a ^ b))
for f in ("seq", "kind", "crc"):
    print("any record carrying %-4s:" % f, any(f in k for k in s))
'

echo "=== 5. the same over the primary checkout working tree, and the two shape SETS compared"
python3 -c '
import json, collections, subprocess
def shapes(lines):
    s = collections.Counter()
    for l in lines:
        l = l.strip()
        if l: s[frozenset(json.loads(l))] += 1
    return s
w = shapes(open("'"$P"'"))
c = shapes(subprocess.run(["git", "show", "0e4324d:domains/modus/cost/0001.ndjson"],
                          capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.splitlines())
print("working-tree records:", sum(w.values()), " distinct key shapes:", len(w))
for f in ("seq", "kind", "crc", "at"):
    print("every working-tree record carries %-4s:" % f, all(f in k for k in w))
print("committed shape SET == working-tree shape SET:", set(c) == set(w))
print("shapes in one corpus and not the other:", [sorted(k) for k in set(c) ^ set(w)])
'

echo "=== 6. never computed, or computed and dropped? same words, different words, control"
echo "--- 6a same words: the search the finding started from"
$G -nc 'crc\|CRC\|crc32' tools/cost-record.py tools/cost_lib.py
echo "grep exit=$?"
$G -n '"seq"\|"kind"\|"crc"' tools/cost-record.py tools/cost_lib.py
echo "grep exit=$?"
echo "--- 6b DIFFERENT words: every integrity primitive a writer could reach for instead"

def drive(label, text, already):
    """`already` is what the records written BEFORE the damage had already billed, so the
    verdict below is derived from the overlap rather than asserted from the label."""
    with open(m.LOG, "w") as fh:

    elif dup == already:

B = ["m1", "m2"]  # families B and C: R1 and R2 had already billed m1 and m2
```

```
=== 1. what doc:40 §2.2 requires, and of which logs
### 2.2 Logs — newline-delimited JSON, append-only <a id="append-only-log"></a>

For high-volume machine data: agent-run output, domain events, cost events, audit trail.
| 2.2.1 | One JSON object per line. No pretty-printing, no embedded newlines (escape them). |
| 2.2.2 | Append-only. A record is **never** modified or deleted in place. A correction is a new record that supersedes an earlier one by `seq`. |
| 2.2.3 | Every record carries a monotonic `seq` (per log), an ISO-8601 UTC `at`, and a `kind`. |
| 2.2.4 | `seq` is the resume cursor for streaming. An SSE `Last-Event-ID` is a `seq`. |
| 2.2.5 | Every record carries `crc`, the CRC-32C of the record's canonical serialisation with the `crc` field itself omitted (§8 makes serialisation deterministic, which is what makes this reproducible on read). `crc` is the last key. |
| 2.2.6 | A record whose line does not parse, lacks `crc`, or whose recomputed `crc` does not match is **torn**: it is skipped on read, reported, and the log is marked `degraded` (§7). It is never repaired and never silently dropped. |
| 2.2.7 | A truncated final line — no trailing newline, at the end of the file — is discarded on read and truncated away before the next append. This is the **only** permitted repair, it applies only to the last line, and it is logged. |
| 2.2.8 | Logs roll at a size threshold into `NNNN.ndjson` segments. Segments are immutable once rolled. |

=== 8. the only reader of the log that exists today, and what it does with a bad line
def last_record_for(run_id):
    """The newest record already written for this run, or None."""
    if not os.path.exists(LOG):
        return None
    seen = None
    with open(LOG) as fh:
        for line in fh:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                rec = json.loads(line)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if rec.get("runId") == run_id and rec.get("lastMessageId"):
                seen = rec
    return seen

--- and the adapter §7 assigns the recovery pass to
      17 adapters/adapter-persistence-flatfile/src/main/kotlin/uk/m4xy/modus/adapter/persistence/flatfile/FlatFilePersistenceAdapter.kt
=== 11. §7's condition table WHOLE — the enumeration is the control for the absence
354:## 7. Crash consistency and recovery
380:## 8. Markdown as both surface and store
| Condition found | Action |
|---|---|
| Orphan `*.tmp` beside a target, older than 1 hour | Delete; log at WARN with the path |
| Orphan `*.tmp` younger than 1 hour | Leave (another process may be mid-write); log at DEBUG |
| Log file whose final line is truncated (no trailing newline) | Truncate to the last complete newline; log at WARN with byte count discarded. Only the final line qualifies (§2.2.7). |
| Log line that fails to parse, or whose `crc` does not match | Skip it, count it, mark the log `degraded`, log at ERROR with the byte offset. **Never repair, never renumber.** A torn record can sit anywhere in the file, not only at the end, so the reader checks every line — a fragment of one record can be followed by a complete later record and then the fragment's tail. |
| Log with a `seq` gap | Log at ERROR; mark the log degraded; do not silently renumber |
| Document failing schema validation | Move to `.modus/quarantine/<timestamp>/`, log at ERROR, continue. **Never** auto-repair. |
| `intent` record with no `completed` | Replay the intent idempotently; append `completed` |
| Stale lock file whose PID is dead | Break; log at WARN |
| Derived index missing, stale, or unreadable | Rebuild from source files |
```

### E1 to E13

**E1 — the rules, and that this log is inside them.** Steps 1, 2, 3 and 18. The bean previously
said *"three independent statements"*. There are five, and they are named rather than counted,
because a count is the one form of this claim a reader cannot check against the corpus
(`doc:50-memory-and-evidence#unverified-shapes`):

- `documentation/40-durability.md:49` — *"Everything durable is one of exactly two shapes. If
  your data does not fit either, you are modelling it wrong."* The strongest of the five: it
  leaves no third shape for a harness-edge log to be. The ledger is a §2.1 document or a §2.2
  log, and it is not a document.
- `documentation/40-durability.md:86` — §2.2's preamble, *"agent-run output, domain events, cost
  events, audit trail"*.
- `documentation/40-durability.md:135` — §3's layout diagram, `cost/0001.ndjson  spend event log`.
- `documentation/40-durability.md:260` — §5's fsync table, *"Cost event log | **Always**, per
  record | Money. Non-negotiable."* Also stronger than the diagram: §5 does not merely name the
  file, it sets a per-record durability policy for it, which is a statement about §2.2 records.
- `documentation/60-cost-model.md:151` — *"(`40-durability.md` §2.2), fsynced per record because
  it is money."*

The layout diagram is the weakest of the five, being a picture of a tree, and the finding does
not rest on it. None of the five admits an exception for a harness-edge writer; E12 takes the
two documents in the corpus that come closest to being one.

**E2 — the key shapes, committed and working-tree, compared as sets.** Steps 4 and 5. Two
distinct shapes at `0e4324d`, of 32 and 34 keys, and the difference between them is printed
rather than described: `the two shapes differ by exactly: ['agentDescription', 'parentRunId']`.
**Two keys, not one.** Over the working tree, `committed shape SET == working-tree shape SET:
True` with `shapes in one corpus and not the other: []`. That is a stronger claim than counting
shapes in each corpus separately: it does not depend on how a shape is described, and a single
shape present in one corpus and not the other would falsify it. `any record carrying` is `False`
for all three fields at the commit and `every record carries` is `False` for all three over the
working tree — asked in both directions because a finding of this shape is falsified by one
counter-example either way.

**E3 — never computed, not computed and dropped.** Step 6, redone. The earlier capture searched
twice with the same word (`crc\|CRC\|crc32`, then `"seq"\|"kind"\|"crc"`) and carried no control.
That is the failure `doc:50-memory-and-evidence#corpus-figures` names — *"A claim of
**absence** needs a second search by different words, and a control."* — and this bean cites
that rule against others while breaking it here. Three searches now:

- **same words** (6a): `grep -c` returns `0` for both tool files; the three quoted key strings
  print nothing and exit 1.
- **different words** (6b): the integrity primitives a writer would reach for instead —
  `hashlib`, `sha256`, `sha1`, `md5`, `checksum`, `digest`, `adler`, `zlib`, `binascii`,
  `hexdigest`. This search **finds hits**, six of them, which is why it was worth running.
  `tools/cost-record.py:28` and `tools/cost_lib.py:14` import `hashlib`; `cost_lib.py:292-297`
  defines `sha256_file`; `cost-record.py:73` hashes the log's *path* to name a lock file. Step 6c
  disposes of them: every caller of `sha256_file` in the tree is in `tools/cost-replay.py`,
  recording input provenance for a replay. Neither use reaches a record. So the conclusion
  survives — but it now survives as a conclusion reached over hits, rather than as a search that
  found nothing.
- **control** (6d): `json` returns 17 and 5, so the search is shown to reach both files. Without
  it, `0` and `0` are equally consistent with having grepped the wrong paths.

**E4 — nothing implements §2.2.4, §2.2.6 or §7's degraded state.** Step 10's recursive search
over every `.kt`, `.ts`, `.tsx` and `.py` file in the tree exits 1 having printed nothing, and
the adapter §7 names is 17 lines. So the resume cursor of §2.2.4 has no consumer, which is the
honest reading of the weakest limb of this finding — and §7 already carries its own
`Enforcement gap:` naming `bean:0017` for the recovery suite that would exercise the rest —
printed at the end of step 11, *"the recovery test suite that would construct each condition
above on disk and assert the exact action taken does not exist. `bean:0017` carries it."*

**E5 — the reader that does exist.** Step 8 is `last_record_for` whole. `except ValueError:
continue` is the §2.2.6 violation, and it is independent of `crc`: the rule requires a skipped
line to be **reported** and the log **marked degraded**, and this does neither.

**E6 — what the damage costs, driven through the real functions.** Step 15 imports
`tools/cost-record.py` with `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` pointed at a scratch directory, so `LOG`
resolves under `$SCRATCH`. That is asserted twice, positively with the resolved path printed
(`LOG is under SCRATCH: True -> [...]/scratchpad/fakerepo/domains/modus/cost/0001.ndjson`) and
negatively against the real path (`LOG is not the real ledger: True`).

The earlier capture drove one damage shape against a one-record log and reported *"bills the run
in full"*. This PR's own `review_focus` raised the right objection to it — whether that
establishes the claim, or only establishes it for a log with exactly one record for the run — and
the answer is the second. It is now a grid: four damage shapes against two log populations, plus
the conflict case in both orderings. The verdict column is derived from the overlap between what
was billed and what the pre-damage records had already billed, not written into the label.

- **Family A — the run's only record is damaged.** All four shapes give
  `cursor=None basis=full billed=3 of 3`, a re-bill of the run in full. The **realistic crash
  shape** — truncated tail, *no* trailing newline, what a crash between `os.write` and
  `os.fsync` leaves — does it exactly as well as the contrived truncate-but-keep-the-newline the
  earlier capture used. So does a hand merge that loses the joining newline, and so does an
  interleaved write from a second appender, which `doc:40-durability` §4.2 states the appender
  lock does not protect against.
- **Family B — an intact earlier record survives.** The same four shapes give
  `cursor=m1 basis=message-cursor billed=2 of 3`: the cursor falls back to the older record and
  `m2` is billed a second time. A **partial** double-bill, and one `advance_cursor` cannot refuse,
  because from its side nothing is wrong — it was handed a cursor and it used it. The refusal
  path `bean:0054` built never comes near this case.
- **Family C — conflict markers, both side orderings.** `C1`, newer record on the HEAD side,
  gives a partial double-bill; `C2`, newer record on the other side, is correct. This corrects
  the earlier capture, which concluded that markers around whole records *"do not lose the
  cursor, they only prove the silent discard"*. That was true of the log it tested, in which both
  sides held the same record. `last_record_for` keeps the **last** matching line it sees, so with
  sides that differ it silently returns whichever the merge put second. Half the orderings
  double-bill, and nothing distinguishes them from the outside.

`A0` and `B0` are the same two logs undamaged and neither double-bills, so the grid is measuring
the damage rather than the harness.

**E7 — three shapes, one writer, no discriminator.** Step 7, recaptured. The earlier capture ran
three different greps, printed four hit lines with `385` on two of them, called that *"three
grep hits"*, and attributed all three wrongly. `grep -n '^ *append('` finds every call site under
one pattern and prints exactly three lines:

- `tools/cost-record.py:217` — the **refusal** record. Step 7's second half prints the two lines
  above it, `if messages is None:` and its comment, which is the branch it sits inside.
- `tools/cost-record.py:382` — `append(record)`, the **spend record**. The earlier pattern
  `append({` could not match this structurally, and the bean never named the line at all.
- `tools/cost-record.py:385` — the **error** record, whose `"at"` is the literal `None`.

Line `219`, which the earlier capture called the refusal call site, is the fifth line of the call
that begins at 217; it appeared in that paste only because a separate grep for
`"billingBasis": "refused"` had been run. `json.dumps` writes 385's `None` as `null`, so a record
exists in this log whose `at` is null while §2.2.3 requires an ISO-8601 UTC `at`. Step 5 reports
`every working-tree record carries at : True` — key presence, not value validity, and the two are
stated separately because the first does not imply the second.

**E8 — `crc` cannot be the last key under this serialiser.** Step 12. `append` calls
`json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True)`; over a five-key sample including the two keys `crc` would
fall between, `crc` lands at index 2 of 5. Any implementation of §2.2.5 here has to either drop
`sort_keys` for a canonical order that ends in `crc`, or amend §2.2.5. Criterion 2 is that
decision.

**E9 — the corpus sweep and its control.** Step 13 names a commit as its subject, so adding this
file to `.beans` does not change it. It returns `modus-0001` — whose lines 186–187, printed at
step 19c, already describe a per-record CRC-32C as *"(`crc`, last key, computed over the
canonical serialisation with `crc` omitted)"* — and `modus-0117`, which recorded this finding
and deferred it. The control returns the two files known to contain `merge=union` at that
commit, so the sweep is shown to reach the corpus it claims to search. Step 14 puts the backlog
this joins at 64 `todo` and 35 `completed` at `0e4324d`; this makes the first number 65 on the
tree that merges it.

**E10 — §2.2.6 and §7 disagree.** Step 11. The **whole** of §7's condition table is printed, not
a selected row, because absence can only be read off a complete enumeration: nine conditions, of
which three concern logs — a truncated final line, a line that *"fails to parse, or whose `crc`
does not match"*, and a *"Log with a `seq` gap"*. No row names a record that lacks `crc`. Two
searches confirm that rather than the eye. The extent is derived inside the step rather than
asserted: the same `grep` prints `354:## 7.` and `380:## 8.`, so §7 runs 354–379, and the `sed`
that follows is bounded by those numbers. Inside it the string `crc` occurs on exactly one line,
the parse/mismatch row. And the word `lacks` occurs exactly **once in the whole
document**, at line `102`, which is §2.2.6. The condition §2.2.6 defines is stated in one section
and absent from the section it delegates its consequence to.

**E11 — the live ledger, and the detector that costs nothing.** Step 16, clock-stamped by its
own trailing `date` at `2026-09-04T09:24:25Z` rather than pinned to a commit, because its subject is the primary
checkout's working tree and that tree grows on every agent run, including the one that took this
figure. 287 records across 51 distinct `runId`s, of which **33 carry exactly one record** — which
is what makes E6's family A the majority case and family B the rest. 51 records are stamped
`billingBasis: full`, one per run. `tools/cost-record.py:277` writes that field straight from
`advance_cursor`'s return (step 19a), which is why a re-bill after a lost cursor is stamped
`full`: ambiguous with a legitimate first record, but not unrecorded. The detector reads that
ambiguity as a check — *a `full` record that is not the first for its `runId`* — and returns
`0 []`. The defect is reachable and has not yet fired, which is a different statement from either
"broken" or "fine", and is the baseline criterion 6 asks for.

**E12 — the two nearest counter-arguments, and why neither is the exception.** Step 17.
`doc:60-cost-model` §3.2.1 exists and is a real, measured harness-edge relaxation — of **§3.2's
field list**, whose excused fields (`stage`, `workItemId`, `rationale`, `priceBookEntryId`) are
the ones a hook cannot observe. `seq`, `kind` and `crc` are not observations of anything; the
writer performs the write and therefore knows them. `adr:0006-framework-boundary#classification`
line 96 does place `tools/` at tier 3, this domain's own workflow — but `doc:40-durability`'s
`read_when` (line 8) selects on `path: "**/*.ndjson"`, the **file** rather than the tool, so §2.2
binds whoever writes such a file whatever tier the writer sits at. `bean:0017`'s reader is tier 1
and will read this tier-3 writer's output.

**E13 — the struck criterion restated a live gate.** Step 19b. `tools/docs-lint.sh:305` opens
check 11 with *"A completed bean is final except for appended amendments"*, classifying each
changed bean by the `status:` it has on the merge base. That is what the struck criterion 9
asserted, in the same words, and it runs inside `bash tools/docs-lint.sh` — which the surviving
criterion 9 requires green.
